description.narrative: General Education Improvement Project (GEIP) is financed by an International Development Association (IDA) Credit (US$60.00 million) and a GPE grant (total amount of Multiplier Maximum Country Allocation of US$9.25 million [after the deduction of the supervision fee for the Grant Agent of US$.075 million]). GPE funding is consisted of US$4.07million (accounting for 44%) for the fixed part and US$5.18 million (accounting for 56%) for the variable part. The World Bank co-financing will fund secondary sub-sector interventions while the GPE funds will support pre-primary and primary education interventions.The project supports main education reform programs of the Royal Government of Cambodia (RGC) as stated in its Education Strategic Plan (ESP) 2019-23 from early childhood education to secondary education sub-sectors. The project includes 420 public secondary schools, 1,000 primary schools, and 213 preschools. Those targeted schools located in all 203 districts in all 25 provinces/capital.The project proposes the following three components: (i) Component 1: Improving Learning Outcomes (63.58 million); Component 2: Strengthening Sector Development and Project Management (US$5.67 million); and (iii) Component 3: Contingent Emergency Response (US$ 0 million). The first component aims to improve teaching and student learning outcomes in target preschools, primary, and secondary schools by (1) supporting the implementation of School-Based Management (SBM); (2) providing capacity development to teachers and school leaders; and (3) improving learning environments. The sub-component 1.3 aims to ensure that general education is available to all students in targeted schools and provide targeted support to stop learning loss from external shocks, such as the COVID-19 pandemic. In particular, this sub-component will support three sets of activities: (i) construction and rehabilitation of schools and labs, training institutions, and dormitories for teachers; (ii) development of specialized environment for students with disabilities, including disability screening; and (iii) a pilot Ed-Tech program for mathematics in secondary school. To address the issues of overcrowded schools and expand access, the project will support (i) rehabilitation of 220 existing school buildings including science laboratory installation; (ii) installation of 80 science laboratories, (iii) construction of 20 new schools in the target districts where new schools are much needed and construction of 100 new school buildings in the existing schools; (iv) construction of PSTTC and TTC; (v) construction of 30 teacher accommodations in remote areas; (vi) construction of two public special education needs school buildings for children with disabilities, and (vii) implementation of Ed-Tech pilot program not only for improving learning outcome by utilizing new technologies, but also for strengthening the resilience of the quality education. The construction/rehabilitation activities will include new or renovated classrooms, age-appropriate furniture, water and sanitation facilities, and accessibility standards for physically disabled children. Water supply (wells or water tanks) will be provided for the latrines, and for hand washing in schools where there is no existing water supply. School Management Committees (SMCs) in all target communities will be trained on school development planning, community participation in procurement, school construction (including ESF instruments and OHS), maintenance, and management using a Construction Manual (CM). The third component is to allow for the reallocation of financing in accordance with the IDA Immediate Response Mechanism in order to provide an immediate response to an eligible crisis or emergency, as needed. Learning from the lessons of the current COVID-19 pandemic, the project will develop CERC Manual and other necessary documents to ensure that CERC can be activated at any time during the emergency.
To improve the quality of and equitable access to general education in target areas, and to provide immediate and effective response in case of an Eligible Crisis or Emergency.

condition.narrative: Annual Works Plans and BudgetsFinancing Agreement: Schedule 2, Section I.C Recurrent, AnnualThe Recipient shall prepare andfurnish to the Association no later than November 30 of each year, an annual work plan and budget containing relevant Projectactivities and expenditures proposed to be included in the Project in the following fiscal year, in a manner and substancesatisfactory to the Association, and thereafter implement the activities under the Project during the relevant fiscal year inaccordance with such plan and budget.

Contingent Emergency ResponseFinancing Agreement: Schedule 2, Section I.F In case of an Eligible Crisis or EmergencyTheRecipient shall (i) adopt a CERC Manual for implementation of Part 3 of the Project and prepare and adopt an Emergency Action Plan;both in form and substance satisfactory to the Association and ensure that the activities under the said part are carried out inaccordance with such manual and plan and all relevant safeguard instruments; and (ii) not amend, waive or abrogate any provisionsof the manual unless the Association agrees otherwise in writing.

Environmental and Social StandardsFinancing Agreement: Schedule 2, Section I.D and Grant Agreement: Schedule 2, SectionIRecurrent, ContinuousThe Recipient shall (i) ensure that the Project is carried out in accordance with the Environmental andSocial Standards and the ESCP (including the management tools and instruments referred to therein) in a manner acceptable to theAssociation; and (ii) not amend, abrogate, repeal, suspend or waive any of their provisions unless the Association agreesotherwise, and report on their status of implementation as part of the project reports.

Institutional ArrangementsFinancing Agreement: Schedule 2, Section I.A Recurrent, ContinuousThe Recipient shall maintain,throughout the Project implementation period, a Project management committee and a Project management team; all with functions,staffing and resources satisfactory to the Association.

Mid-term Review Financing Agreement: Schedule 2, Section II.B and Grant Agreement: Schedule 2, Section IOnce, 30 months after theEffective Date The Recipient shall prepare and furnish to the Association a mid-term report in form and substance satisfactory tothe Association.

PBC Monitoring and ReportingFinancing Agreement: Schedule 2, Section I.E and Grant Agreement: Schedule 2, Section IRecurrent,Continuous/ Due date: Six (6) months after the Effective DateThe Recipient shall appoint an Independent Verification Agency tocarry out independent verification of the status of achievement of PBC TargetsRecurrent, Continuous/ Due date: February 28annuallyThe Recipient shall furnish reports to the Association on the status of achievement of the relevant PBC Targets.

Project Operations ManualFinancing Agreement: Schedule 2, Section I.B Recurrent, ContinuousThe Recipient shall carry out theProject in accordance with the Project Operations Manual, and not amend, waive or abrogate any provisions of the manual unless theAssociation agrees otherwise in writing.
